input.summary: The packet contains a synthetic claim about TCP flow completion time under emulated bottleneck conditions with and without 20 ms added delay. The packet fields (problem, conditions, inputs, metrics, controls, design, alternatives, limitations) are all empty, and no protocol exists. Three key decisions are needed before a complete pilot can be drafted: (1) what specific emulated network configuration and traffic parameters will be used, (2) what input trace or workload will drive the TCP flows, and (3) what resource budget (time, replications) is available. Critically, the user's question asks whether a single emulated trial can "prove causality for all Internet users" — this conflates a descriptive pilot with causal inference and population generalization, neither of which is authorized by the descriptive-only policy or achievable by emulation alone.
clarification_questions: What specific emulated network configuration should be used (e.g., bottleneck bandwidth, queue discipline, topology), and what TCP flow workload or traffic trace will serve as the input — are these available as versioned files with known SHA-256 hashes?
How many replications and what wall-clock time budget are available for this pilot, and is the intended runner 'emulated-netem-v1'?
Should the pilot measure one-way flow completion time or round-trip, and what is the precise unit of observation (e.g., per-flow, per-experiment run)?

proposal.problem: The packet fields describing the experimental setup are entirely empty; no inputs, configurations, metrics, controls, or resource limits have been specified. A descriptive pilot cannot be fully drafted without these details.
proposal.question: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, does adding 20 ms delay produce an observable difference in TCP flow completion time compared to a no-added-delay baseline, as measured in a controlled emulated network environment?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions are implied: (1) baseline — fixed emulated bottleneck with no added delay; (2) treatment — same bottleneck with 20 ms one-way (or round-trip, to be resolved) delay added via network emulation. Exact bandwidth, queue discipline, and topology remain unspecified.
proposal.related_work: The source citation is synthetic and unreviewed; no full text or prior measurements are available. No citations are invented here.
proposal.alternatives: Alternative explanations for any observed difference include queue-induced delay at the bottleneck, TCP congestion-control interactions with the emulated delay, and variability in flow start timing — none can be ruled out by a descriptive pilot alone.
proposal.design: A descriptive pilot comparing TCP flow completion time across the two delay conditions using an emulated network runner. Causal attribution to the delay manipulation and generalization to real Internet users are not supported by emulation alone and are outside the scope of this descriptive pilot.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: TCP flow completion time (units to be confirmed as milliseconds or seconds). Secondary: any recorded throughput or retransmission counts if available from the runner.
proposal.controls: Fixed bottleneck bandwidth, queue discipline, flow size, and TCP implementation version should be held constant across conditions. Randomization of condition order and replication count remain unspecified.
proposal.inputs: No versioned input files or SHA-256 hashes have been provided. Traffic workload, topology configuration files, and emulation parameter files are all unknown and must be supplied before execution.
proposal.limitations: Emulation results cannot establish real-world performance, causality, or generalization to all Internet users. A single trial cannot prove any causal claim. Missing packet fields prevent a complete pilot specification at this time.
